en: We then, for example, also have the list.ts
file, which we use for listing files because
Bun's S3 client can of course not just be
used for uploading files, but also for
downloading and listing files.
Listing is done by using the S3 client and
then its list method. So before we had the
file method to get hold of a remote file on
which we wanna operate, but we can also
directly on the client call list to list all
files in a bucket.
And list takes some settings like a prefix
for filtering, so that you can only list all
the files in a certain path on that remote
bucket, how many files it should return in
one list attempt. The default is 1,000 keys,
but you can limit that,
and therefore you need pagination if you
have potentially more
keys, more files on that remote host than
that.
And the continuation token is needed for
that pagination where you may have more than
1,000 or max keys objects on that remote
host. That simply is used to know after
which file to continue with listing. But
that list function then contains the entire
logic for listing and for,
if needed, paginating and going through all
the files on that remote host.
And of course, we also might want to
restore. So we want to download files. And
again, we do this through the client there.
If we wanna restore a file, we get hold of
it, get hold of the remote file with the
file method as before, but then we first
check whether it exists because obviously we
can only restore what exists on the remote
host. And if it does, we create the folder
that may be needed locally
and write that local file with the Bun.write
API, which is now the local Bun file API.
And that's how we write that file. And the
convenient thing about the Bun.write
API or the Bun local file API in general is
that you can pass that remote file handle as
a value here.
So you may remember from earlier in the
course that the values you pass to Write as
a second argument are the content of the
file and that could be a blob, that could be
a string if you're writing a text file, but
it can also be an S3 file handle, a remote
file handle, and Bun will then automatically
download that file and put its content into
that local file. That's super convenient, of
course.
Now, if we chose to
restore an entire folder, we do that by
again listing and paginating if needed.
Since that folder may of course contain
multiple files, potentially more than are
returned by one list statement.
And then we just go through all these files
and download them step by step, same
approach as before, now just with multiple
files instead of one.
By the way, if you have such a remote file
and you don't wanna write it to a file like
this,
you could also get the text of that remote
file if it is
a file that contains text by calling the
text method on that remote file handle and
awaiting that promise and that gives you the
file content as a string. But again, only if
that remote file contains something that
makes sense as a string, of course.
But then you can use that string here
however you want. You can write it to a
local file, you can console.log it, whatever
you want. That's worth knowing too. But if
you wanna store a remote file locally,
that's the way to go, using Bun's localWrite
API,
the target file, the local file, and then a
pointer at the remote file.
